statement: A shape on squared paper slides 3 squares right and 2 squares down. Then it slides 1 square left and 4 squares up. Where is it now, compared with where it started?

choices.misconception: I treated the slide to the left as another slide to the right.
I added the 2 down and the 4 up together instead of letting them cancel.
I only used the second slide and forgot about the first one.
I took 2 away from 4 correctly but kept the direction of the first slide, which was down.

hints: Deal with left-right and up-down separately.
A slide is a translation: combine the sideways moves, then the up-down moves. Moves in opposite directions cancel each other out.
Sideways: 3 right and 1 left. Up and down: 2 down and 4 up.

solutions.reliable: Sideways: 3 right then 1 left leaves 3 - 1 = 2 squares right. Up and down: 2 down then 4 up leaves 4 - 2 = 2 squares up. So the shape is 2 squares right and 2 squares up from where it started. The transferable idea: two slides together make one slide, found by combining the across moves and the up-down moves separately.

whyOnTest: Combining slides tests whether opposite moves are seen to cancel, which underlies every grid and coordinate problem.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
